S36.02.needs: an answer that uses web search; a network connection
S36.02.note: If a source has no title, the code shows the site host instead (sources.ts line 31 falls back to sourceHost). The web-search route is needed to produce sources; I did not confirm which plans have it.
steps: Sign in and ask a question that gets a web-sourced answer (one that uses web search).
Under the answer, click the button that reads "N sources" (N is the number of sources).
Look at each item in the list: each should show a bold title line (the source title) with the site name above it.
Hover a numbered or site-name citation chip in the answer text and check that its card shows the same title for each source.
Compare with Expected: each cited source shows its title.
S36.02.where: Chat answer with web sources > click the "$COUNT$ sources" button under the answer (shows as e.g. "5 sources") > list of sources; also hover or tap an inline citation chip to see its card

S36.03.needs: an answer that uses web search; a network connection
S36.03.note: The site name is the source URL's host without www (sources.ts line 11 and 28); the visible text is the domain itself, so there is no fixed English word for it. The "$SITE$ +$COUNT$" label is only the grouped chip form; a single-source chip shows the bare domain.
steps: Ask a question that gets a web-sourced answer.
Find the small citation chip in the answer text. A chip with more than one source reads with the site name and "+N".
Hover the chip (or tap it on a touch screen) and read the card: each source has a small globe icon and a site name line above its title.
Click the "N sources" button under the answer and check the site name line on each item.
Compare with Expected: each cited source shows its publisher or site name (domain without www).
S36.03.where: Chat answer with web sources > inline citation chip (site name with "+N" when grouped) > hover or tap the chip; also the "$COUNT$ sources" button under the answer

S36.04.needs: an answer that uses web search; a network connection
S36.04.note: The URL itself is not printed as text; it is the link target (bubbles.ts lines 866-872 only allow http and https links in the activity step; sources.ts uses source.url directly for answer citations). The tester must check the new tab's address to confirm the URL.
steps: Ask a question that gets a web-sourced answer.
Click the "N sources" button under the answer to open the list.
Click a source's title: a new browser tab should open at that address.
Optionally, in an agent run that searched the web, click the step row "Sources for ..." to expand it, then click a source link; it should open in a new tab.
Compare with Expected: each cited source exposes its URL and opens when clicked.
S36.04.where: Chat answer with web sources > click the "$COUNT$ sources" button under the answer > click a source title (opens in a new tab). Also Activity step "Sources for $QUERY$" in the agent steps (click the step row to expand it, then click a source)
